details: A modified fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web API library that silently enrolls the installer's WhatsApp account into four fixed channels owned by the package author. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js, inside makeNewsletterSocket(), two injected setTimeout blocks wait 90 seconds and then send newsletter "FOLLOW" queries over the already-authenticated WhatsApp socket (via the w:mex GraphQL endpoint), each scheduling a second follow 5 seconds later. The target channel JIDs are hidden as base64 string literals, and each call is wrapped in an empty try/catch so it fails invisibly: 120363400706010828@newsletter, 120363423257544642@newsletter, 120363349457176430@newsletter and 120363421052027188@newsletter. The 90-second delay places the action after library load, once the session is live. A fifth hardcoded channel, 120363402220977044@newsletter ("Queen Jusmy Md"), is stamped into forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo and newsletter contextInfo in lib/Utils/messages.js and lib/Socket/luxu.js so outgoing messages carry the author's channel branding. Nothing in the package documents these subscriptions or offers a way to disable them; they are not opt-in. The package does not steal WhatsApp session credentials, tokens, environment variables or files — its network traffic is confined to WhatsApp/Meta endpoints — the abuse is the covert, non-consensual subscription of the user's account.
